action: As Osaka University warns, be alert to suspicious emails that may be sent to the leaked addresses.
date_note: Date Osaka University announced the leak, per Nikkei's article of that day; the unauthorized access to Arara was on 28 October.
exec: A mail-delivery contractor's breach exposed 51,891 email addresses of a university's students and staff, raising the risk of suspicious emails.
geo_basis: Osaka University, named in the source (city of Suita/Osaka area; pinned at Osaka)
plain: Osaka University says 51,891 email addresses of students and staff leaked after unauthorized access at Arara, the company that sends emails for its safety-confirmation system. Other data such as names was not confirmed leaked.
summary: Nikkei reports Osaka University announced on 27 November that 51,891 email addresses of students and staff leaked. It says the cause was unauthorized access on 28 October to Arara, the contractor that delivers email for the university's safety-confirmation system. Nikkei says no other information, such as names or affiliations, has been confirmed leaked, and the university suspended the system.
title: Osaka University says 51,891 student and staff email addresses leaked via Arara unauthorized access

validation.note: Single source: Nikkei's report of the university's announcement; the university's own notice was not found or read.

evidence.quote: 大阪大学は27日、学生と教職員のメールアドレスが5万1891件漏洩したと発表した。
